metadata.title: Storybook Modernization Tasks
metadata.description: Move Daedalus off Storybook 6.4.22, storiesOf() and addon-knobs onto 10.6.x by way of 8.6.x, then cover every router-reachable screen with a container story built on one shared MobX store fixture harness
metadata.importantNote: yarn storybook:build is a required CI check (perSystem/checks.nix:78, x86_64-linux only) and is the only automated check that renders components with real themes and translations. The trunk must never carry a commit with it red. Phase 3 is the one landing that cannot be decomposed into smaller green commits, and the constraint is yarn compile rather than the build: at 8.6.x a file still importing storiesOf from @storybook/react fails tsc whether or not the indexer sees it, and tsconfig.json declares no include, so every story file is in the program. It is therefore landed as a single merge from a single branch that is green when it merges. Phases 6 and 7 are additive and cannot break an existing story.

phases.name: Baseline, Deletions And Version-Neutral Changes
phases.description: Everything that can land on the pinned Storybook 6.4.22 without touching a story shape. Records the sidebar baseline the whole conversion is diffed against, removes the story sets the owner has decided to delete, removes the /staking/epochs screen and the dead /redeem-itn-wallets route binding, and lands the standalone tsconfig change.

tasks.title: Capture the sidebar baseline
tasks.description: Record the full sidebar tree as it stands before any change: 15 top-level groups, 53 distinct panel titles and 272 registrations with their display labels, 267 under storybook/stories and 5 in the colocated story files. A raw grep for .add( over storybook/stories returns 272; three of those are moment().add() chains at staking/_support/Epochs.tsx:10, staking/_support/Undelegate.tsx:108 and staking/_support/DelegationSteps.tsx:211, and two more sit in the support module governance/_utils/drepPopulation.ts, which registers nothing. Every later label check is a diff against this file, because the codemod sanitizer renames 80 exports and a wrong sidebar label is invisible to every automated check.
implementationNotes: Build the workbench and walk the sidebar, or extract the titles from the storiesOf() and .add() arguments; both are acceptable as long as the result records group, panel and story label for every registration.
Store the baseline as a plain text or JSON file outside the repository, or as a scratch artifact attached to the branch. It is a working reference, not a deliverable.
Record the count alongside the tree so a missing registration shows up as an arithmetic difference rather than a reading error.
acceptance: Every one of the 272 registrations across the 84 story files appears in the baseline with its group, panel and label
The baseline distinguishes the two registrations in staking/Legacy.stories.tsx that the barrel never loads
tasks.notes: Cheap, and the whole conversion is unverifiable without it.

tasks.title: Delete the orphaned legacy staking story and its eight components
tasks.description: Locked decision 5. storybook/stories/staking/Legacy.stories.tsx is unreachable from the barrel, so its two registrations never appear in the sidebar and storybook:build never loads it. It is also the only reference in the repository to source/renderer/app/components/staking/legacy/.
implementationNotes: Confirm the components are unreferenced before deleting: grep for each of the eight component names across source/, storybook/ and tests/.

The directory carries a .scss stylesheet alongside each component plus the _stakingConfig.scss partial, 17 tracked files in all. The .scss.d.ts files are not among them: .gitignore:141 ignores *.scss.d.ts and typed-scss-modules generates them through the precompile script, so none is tracked anywhere in the repository and none is part of this commit. Note also that two partials are named _stakingConfig.scss. Only the copy inside legacy/ goes; source/renderer/app/components/staking/_stakingConfig.scss at the parent level has at least five surviving importers and is untouched.
tsc is the only thing that has been compiling these files, because tsconfig.json declares no include and only excludes node_modules.

This task changes four tracked i18n artifacts, which the entry did not previously say. StakingChartTooltip.tsx is the only file in the directory calling defineMessages, and its six ids under staking.chart.tooltip.* appear in translations/messages.json, i18n/locales/defaultMessages.json, en-US.json and ja-JP.json. The i18n check at perSystem/checks.nix:64-76 regenerates and requires no diff, so removing the component without regenerating leaves a required check red. Regenerate in the same commit; all six carry the !!! untranslated prefix in both locales, so no translation is lost.

Refinement to locked decision 5, which records five components as referenced by nothing at all. Measured: legacy/Staking.tsx is referenced by nothing, and BlockGenerationInfo, StakingSwitch and StakingSystemState are referenced only by it, with StakingSystemStateElement referenced only by StakingSystemState. It is one dead subtree rooted at an unreferenced file rather than five isolated files. Same conclusion, and it is what a reviewer re-running the per-component greps will see.
acceptance: yarn storybook:build, yarn compile and yarn lint pass

ROUTES.REDEEM_ITN_REWARDS at routes-config.ts:4 goes with it. Routes.tsx:211 is its only reader, and a path constant with no binding is the same trap in a smaller form: a goToRoute written against it gives a blank content area rather than an error.

tasks.title: Rename the 15 sibling-registering story files out of the convention
tasks.description: Fifteen files match the *.stories.* naming convention and register no stories of their own; they import or re-export siblings. Move them into _support/ and rename them so the phase 2 glob cannot pick them up as indexer inputs. At 6.4.22 the glob would auto-title them and register their named exports, moving the phase 1 sidebar baseline; at 8.6 and 10.6 they are a hard build-storybook failure via NoMetaError collected into MultipleIndexingError.
implementationNotes: WalletSettingsScreen.stories.tsx:139 has a default export, but it is an anonymous React component rather than a CSF meta object, so it registers nothing and belongs in this set.
Status.stories.ts is a single line: import './Diagnostics.stories';. AddWallet.stories.ts is five such lines.
Renaming is chosen over a glob exclusion so the trap is not left in place for the sixteenth such file, and over adding default exports so the sidebar does not gain roughly 15 panels nobody asked for.
Update every importer. task-010 replaces the barrel, so an import that breaks here surfaces immediately rather than at the glob.
acceptance: No file under storybook/stories matches *.stories.* without either a storiesOf call or a CSF default export whose value is a meta object
yarn compile passes, proving no importer was left dangling

phases.name: Story Indexing
phases.description: Replace the hand-maintained barrel with a glob on the pinned 6.4.22, so that an unreferenced story file becomes a build participant instead of a silent absence, and so the required check's coverage matches the corpus before the conversion starts.

tasks.title: Replace the barrel with a glob and rehome its side effects
tasks.description: storybook/main.ts:8 declares stories: ['../storybook/stories/index.ts'], a barrel of side-effect imports. Replace it with a glob over the story file naming conventions, and move the two side effects at storybook/stories/index.ts:1-2, the global SCSS import and the environment import, into preview.
implementationNotes: The glob must match both naming conventions in use: *.stories.ts, *.stories.tsx and *.story.tsx, and must reach the four colocated files under source/renderer/app.
Storybook 6 has supported glob stories entries since 6.0 and loads a storiesOf file found by a glob exactly as the barrel did, because registration is a side effect of loading the module either way.
If 6.4.22's indexer rejects the glob, fold this task and task-011 into phase 3 and verify them at 8.6.x instead. Nothing later in the plan depends on where the glob is verified.
Delete storybook/stories/index.ts only once the side effects are rehomed and the build is green.
The barrel currently also loads sibling-registering modules; the 15 files that register no stories of their own must still be reachable from the file that registers their exports.

Why this is a coverage increase rather than a configuration tidy-up, since several later entries carry the opposite inference: yarn compile does not report an unresolvable relative import in this repository, measured during task-006 with a probe and recorded in task-062-impl-review.md. yarn storybook:build does report one, but only for a module the indexer reaches. Under the barrel that was whatever someone remembered to list, which is how Legacy.stories.tsx stayed dead for years with every check green. Under the glob it is the corpus on disk.

The two side effects this entry asks to move into preview were already there, at preview.tsx:4 and :6. What the task actually requires is to stop loading the barrel duplicates. The two stylesheet imports were not equivalent: the barrel used a plain specifier, which goes through the .scss rule in webpackFinal where css-loader has modules enabled with localIdentName and therefore rewrites every class name in a stylesheet whose entire purpose is to be global; preview.tsx uses an inline style-loader!css-loader!sass-loader chain that bypasses the rule and emits the names unchanged. Deleting the barrel removes the scoped duplicate and keeps the correct one. This is the one change here with a possible visual consequence and it cannot be seen from a build: the symptom to look for is unstyled previews across every story, and the cause would be this line.

The glob also orphans two of the 15 files task-062 renamed, nodes/status/_support/Status.ts and wallets/addWallet/_support/AddWallet.ts. Both are import-only barrels whose single importer was a sub-barrel removed here, and the story files they reached are matched by the glob directly. task-062 recorded in advance that this task would remove them. The other 13 keep their importers.

task-001-sidebar-extract.js rooted its reachability walk at the barrel and had to be updated in this task, since that file no longer exists. Its roots are now every file matching the story naming convention under the two directories the globs name. The output format is unchanged and the artifact it produces is byte-identical across this change. Note that the reachability column is now close to tautological for a registering file, because the glob matches all of them; the guarantee it used to provide has moved into the build, which is the point of the phase.
acceptance: yarn storybook:build, yarn compile and yarn lint pass
Every story file on disk is indexed, verified by count against task-001
The frozen clock in storybook/preview.tsx still applies

tasks.title: Make the sidebar grouping and ordering explicit
tasks.description: Sidebar order is currently implicit in barrel import order. Under a glob it becomes whatever the indexer produces unless it is stated, so encode it through the title values and a storySort in preview parameters.
implementationNotes: 14 top-level groups and 49 panel titles, not the 15 and 53 first recorded here: phase 1 removed three panels in task-002, removed the root-level StakingChart group in task-003, and added a registration to an existing panel in task-006. Note also that the task-001 baseline records no order at all. That was deliberate, and task-001.md says so: order at 6.4.22 was implicit in barrel import order and the plan intended to replace the barrel, so capturing it would have encoded the thing being changed. The acceptance criterion is therefore met by its second limb, a deliberate order that is written down.
storySort accepts an explicit order array; prefer that over a comparator so the intended order is readable.

The order chosen is the one the barrel produced, recovered rather than invented. At 6.4.22 storiesOf registers as a side effect of module evaluation and the barrel evaluated its imports depth-first in source order, so a depth-first walk of the import graph at 5311ce0d0, the last commit before task-010, reproduces the sequence users saw: Nodes, Loading, Wallets, Decentralization, dApps, Voting, Governance, Settings, Assets, News, Navigation, Common, Discreet Mode, Analytics.

One difference from the barrel era is accepted and recorded. storySort returns 0 for two stories sharing a title unless includeNames is set, and sortStoriesV6 then breaks the tie on fileNameOrder, which under the glob is require.context order. Seven of the 49 panels are assembled from more than one file and hold 45 of the 258 registrations between them: Wallets / Settings (7 files), Wallets / Add Wallet (5), Wallets / Transactions (4), News / Overlays (3), Wallets / Tokens (3), Navigation / Sidebar (2) and Wallets / Summary (2). In those seven, story order is now file path order. Pinning it would need includeNames plus an order array naming all 258 stories, regenerated by hand whenever a story is added, which defeats the readability this entry asks for. The other 42 panels come from one file each and keep their in-file definition order.

Verified without a browser by running the shipped comparator. storySort is a pure function exported from the installed @storybook/store; feeding it the 258 extracted registrations together with the order array read out of preview.tsx reproduces the group and panel sort the preview performs, and the 49 titles come out in exactly the barrel-era sequence. storybook:build passing only proves the parameter parses.
acceptance: The sidebar order matches the task-001 baseline, or every difference is deliberate and recorded
yarn storybook:build passes

tasks.title: Verify the glob against the baseline
tasks.description: Confirm that the corpus the indexer sees is the corpus on disk. This is the point at which the silent-absence defect that killed Legacy.stories.tsx is fixed.
implementationNotes: Compare the registration count against the baseline. The expected figure is 258, not the 257 first recorded here. The subtraction behind 257 is right as far as it goes, the task-001 baseline of 272 less the 15 registrations phase 1 removed, 12 in task-002, 2 in task-003 and 1 in task-004. It omits the one registration task-006 added, Wallets / Settings | Undelegate Wallet. 272 - 15 + 1 = 258. Stated here so the next reader does not re-derive 257 from the same subtraction. The count is established by composition rather than read out of a running workbench, which this environment cannot open: task-010 showed the require.context matchers select exactly the 65 convention-following files on disk, and those 65 carry 258 registrations.

Add a temporary story file in a directory no barrel ever referenced, confirm it appears, then remove it. Two things make this test mean something. Put it under source/renderer/app/components/widgets: that half of the glob holds 1508 tracked files and 4 stories, so it is where an indexing failure would be least visible, and no barrel ever named it. And do not treat a green build as evidence it was indexed, because a file the indexer ignores also builds green. Run it both ways: with the probe valid and present the build must be green, and with an unresolvable import added to that same file it must go red. The green run is what makes the red one attributable to the import rather than to the file. Done here: the matcher selected the path, the extractor count rose 258 to 259, the valid probe built green, the broken one failed with Can't resolve './GlobCheckProbeMissing', and after removal the corpus returned to 258. That is the silent-absence defect shown closed rather than assumed closed.
acceptance: The indexed registration count equals the expected 257
A story file added anywhere under the globbed paths appears without a further edit

tasks.title: Replace withState with a local wrapper and remove @dump247/storybook-state
tasks.description: @dump247/storybook-state imports @storybook/addons (dist/index.js:11) and calls addons.getChannel() at :157 at module-evaluation time, and it peers @storybook/addons ^3.2.16. Phase 3 removes @storybook/addons and no version of it exists in the 8 line. Replace the 17 withState call sites with a local stateful wrapper component that touches no Storybook API, then drop the dependency, so the hop in phase 3 carries nothing that cannot survive it.
implementationNotes: The wrapper holds React state and passes it plus a setter to the render function. No Storybook channel, no addon registration, no decorator.
It is version-agnostic by construction, so it works identically on 6.4.22 and 8.6.x and is deleted in phase 4 when these sites become useArgs.

Keeping 6.4.22's @storybook/addons instead does not work: dist/cjs/index.js:143 keys its singleton on __STORYBOOK_ADDONS and :49-56 throws 'Accessing non-existent addons channel' when setChannel was never called, which Storybook 8 never does.

Installing @storybook/addons@7.6.x does not work either: its module.exports is a named re-export set with no default export carrying getChannel, and it drags a 7.x runtime into a Yarn 1 flat-hoisted tree.

tasks.title: Pre-flight Storybook 8.6.x against React 16.14.0 in a scratch worktree
tasks.description: Storybook's React 16 support is a peer-range commitment, not proof that every code path was exercised at 16.14.0. implementationNotes: Scratch worktree, not the working branch. Nothing from this task is merged.

Carry all four legacy-decorator settings across: tsconfig.json:17 experimentalDecorators, storybook/main.ts:79 parser decorators, storybook/main.ts:84 legacyDecorator, storybook/main.ts:87 useDefineForClassFields.

Include one story that mounts react-polymorph through StoryDecorator's ThemeProvider with SimpleSkins and SimpleDefaults. react-polymorph 1.0.4 was last published 2022-04-14, sits between Storybook and every rendered story, and has not been exercised under a modern preview runtime.
Include one MobX observing component so a silent decorator regression surfaces here rather than three tranches into the conversion.
Include one story that uses the full StoryProvider and StoryLayout shell.

Confirm the webpackFinal body carries over unchanged: the SWC rule, SCSS modules with the [name]_[local] local ident, .inline.svg via svg-inline-loader, the two NormalModuleReplacementPlugin rules for @trezor/transport, the nine Node polyfills and the five stubbed modules.

Confirm withKnobs is still callable as a plain function at 8.0.1. 22 sites use the withKnobs(story, context) idiom rather than registering it as a decorator, for example storybook/stories/wallets/_utils/WalletsWrapper.tsx:9. This is not the documented usage and cannot be assumed to survive the version bump. Discovering it inside phase 3 means discovering it inside the one landing that cannot be decomposed.

RESULT, blocking deviation found. The repository webpackFinal assigns config.resolve wholesale rather than merging into it. At 6.4.22 that costs nothing. At 8.6.x it breaks React 16 outright: @storybook/react-dom-shim ships its own webpackFinal preset that sets resolve.alias["@storybook/react-dom-shim"] to its react-16 build whenever react-dom is below 18, and assigning over config.resolve discards that alias, so the preview tries to resolve react-dom/client, which does not exist in React 16.14.0. Observed as SB_BUILDER-WEBPACK5_0002 Module not found: Can't resolve react-dom/client. The fix, verified in the pre-flight, is to spread: config.resolve = { ...config.resolve, extensions: [...new Set([...(config.resolve.extensions||[]), ...ours]), fallback: { ...config.resolve.fallback, ...ours } }. task-015 must carry this or the hop cannot build at all.

RESULT, kill criterion not triggered. react-polymorph 1.0.4 renders correctly under the 8.6.18 preview pipeline at React 16.14.0. Input and Button both render through StoryDecorator ThemeProvider with SimpleSkins and SimpleDefaults, carry their values and labels, and receive theme class names. The full shell, StoryDecorator wrapping StoryProvider, mounts and renders a story inside it. Ten render assertions, all passing.

RESULT, MobX. An @observable mutated inside runInAction re-renders an @observer story: count:0 to count:1. The pre-flight compiles with the same four legacy-decorator settings the repository uses and reproduces configure({ enforceActions: observed }). This is the assertion that would fail if a decorator setting were dropped, since that failure is a runtime one.

RESULT, withKnobs at @storybook/addon-knobs 8.0.1. The corpus idiom works. Calling withKnobs(story, context) from inside a decorator, exactly as storybook/stories/wallets/_utils/WalletsWrapper.tsx:9 does, renders the wrapped story and the knobs return their defaults. Called bare outside a story render it throws "Storybook preview hooks can only be called inside decorators and story functions", which is expected rather than a regression: the addon uses preview hooks internally and needs an active hook context. An earlier pre-flight attempt that called it bare recorded a false negative.

RESULT, story signatures at 8.6.18, measured rather than assumed. The first render argument is the args object and the second is the full story context. A story written (props) => props.currentTheme therefore reads args and gets undefined unless currentTheme is declared as an arg; a story written (_, props) => props.currentTheme reads the context. The rule for the conversion follows: do not rewrite a first-argument site to read the context, because that is a behaviour change rather than a fix and a visual diff would flag it as a regression. task-016 moves theme, locale and OS to globals, which live at context.globals, so second-argument sites migrate there and first-argument sites need a per-site decision recorded in their tranche.

RESULT, environment. The npm registry is reachable, so this ran here rather than needing an operator. @storybook/react and @storybook/react-webpack5 8.6.18 peer react ^16.8.0, and @storybook/addon-knobs stops at 8.0.1, whose four ^8.0.0 peers all publish 8.6.18. @storybook/test is an optional peer of @storybook/react and its absence is a build warning, not an error. LIMIT. Rendering was established through composeStories from @storybook/react 8.6.18 under jsdom, which applies the project annotations, decorators and parameters, plus a successful storybook build. There is no display here, so the manager, the addon panels and the iframe bootstrap are not covered. That is the same blind spot locked decision 7 records; this narrows it rather than closing it.

implementationNotes: Run storiesof-to-csf, then csf-hoist-story-annotations, then csf-2-to-3 from the 8.6.x CLI over one real domain, in the scratch worktree.

Record what it actually produced: how many files converted cleanly, how many exports the sanitizer renamed, what the display-name re-attachment looks like, and how much hand correction each file needed.

The chain reported 1 ok, 0 errors and produced a file carrying 14 of 19 registrations, losing exactly the five non-literal labels Delegation Center, Pools Index, Pools Index - Loading, Rewards and Stake Pools List. The corpus is 68 storiesOf() calls across 65 files, not 73; 73 was the pre-phase-1 figure and phase 1 removed six calls while task-006 added one. RESULT: no file is skipped for want of a string-literal title and none already has a default export. But three files hold TWO storiesOf calls, nodes/status/Diagnostics.stories.tsx, staking/Staking.stories.tsx and voting/Voting.stories.tsx, and the codemod emits one export default per call, so each produces a file with two default exports, which is not valid TypeScript. RESULT over the dry-run tranche, nodes plus settings, 9 files and 28 registrations: storiesof-to-csf 0 errors 9 ok, csf-hoist-story-annotations 0 errors 3 ok 6 unmodified, csf-2-to-3 0 errors 4 ok 5 unmodified. Per-file hand correction cost: zero for 8 of 9, one file split for the ninth.

DECISION on the kill criterion: not triggered, the codemod is used for the whole corpus. 62 of 65 files convert with zero hand correction and no label loss. Three need a mechanical split first and one of those also needs five labels inlined. The procedure for each tranche is therefore: split any file with more than one storiesOf call, inline any non-literal .add() label, run the chain, then diff the tranche label set against the task-001 baseline. That last step is not optional: it is the only thing that catches a dropped registration.

RESULT on the four control-flow strings. context.kind and context.story are both still populated at 8.6.18, carrying the title and the story name, so the sites survive the version hop itself. tasks.title: Run the codemod chain over the whole corpus
tasks.description: Apply storiesof-to-csf, csf-hoist-story-annotations and csf-2-to-3 across every remaining story file, producing the mechanical half of the conversion in one reviewable commit.
implementationNotes: PRECONDITIONS, both already satisfied on the branch before the hop opened. task-014 found two ways the codemod damages this corpus, and both remedies were landed while the branch was still green because they are version-independent and doing them inside the red window would be strictly worse. First, a file with two storiesOf calls converts to a file with two export default statements, which is not valid TypeScript; the three such files were split into one file per title, adding voting/VotingInfo.stories.tsx, nodes/status/MithrilPartialSyncConfirmation.stories.tsx and staking/RedeemItnRewards.stories.tsx, with the shared staking decorator moved to staking/_support/decorator.tsx and the shared voting fixture to voting/_support/fundInfo.ts. Second, the codemod silently drops a .add() whose label is not a string literal; the five such labels in staking/Staking.stories.tsx were inlined. Verified after: no file holds more than one storiesOf call and no registration carries a non-literal label, so this task now runs against a corpus with zero known conversion defects.
Run the chain from the 8.6.x CLI, in the order the migration guide documents. Running csf-2-to-3 before csf-hoist-story-annotations produces a shape the later transform cannot read.

Reach the four colocated files under source/ as well: components/profile/analytics/Analytics.stories.tsx, components/wallet/tokens/wallet-token-picker/WalletTokenPicker.stories.tsx, features/discreet-mode/ui/DiscreetValue.story.tsx, features/discreet-mode/ui/discreet-toggle/DiscreetModeToggle.story.tsx.
Commit the raw codemod output before hand-finishing anything, so the hand corrections are reviewable separately from the mechanical transform.
Run nix fmt over the result. Formatting is not negotiable and the codemod does not produce prettier-clean output.

Measure this task by the label set diffed against the task-001 baseline, not by the codemod exit status. task-014 established that the chain reports 1 ok, 0 errors while discarding registrations, so a clean run says nothing about whether stories survived. The same applies to every hand-finish tranche.

RESULT. All 68 story files converted, 64 under storybook/stories and 4 colocated under source/renderer/app. Every stage reported 0 errors and 0 skipped, no warning was emitted, and no file imports storiesOf any more. nix fmt was run over the result and the commit carries no hand edits.

MEASUREMENT. The label set is unchanged. 258 registrations across 49 panels before; 258 across 49 after by an AST reading that resolves each export's effective label the way Storybook does; 258 entries across 49 titles after by index.json from a real Storybook build, which is Storybook's own indexer rather than a model of it. The three sets are identical pair for pair, not merely equal in size. Per file the title and the ordered sequence of labels are identical for all 68, so no panel was reordered. 151 of the 258 come back with an explicit name, each one a display name the export identifier cannot spell; those are the population task-023 checks individually.

CORRECTION. The first run converted 1 of the 64 files under storybook/stories and reported 'Applying storiesof-to-csf: 1 files ... 0 errors, 1 ok'. storybook migrate re-launches itself as npx @storybook/cli migrate through child_process.spawn with shell: true, so the --glob value is pathname-expanded by /bin/sh before the CLI parses arguments. /bin/sh has no globstar, so a/**/*.stories.tsx collapsed to a/*/*.stories.tsx, the first match became the value of --glob and the other 63 became positional arguments the CLI ignores. The dry run over a copy had not shown it: there the collapsed pattern matched nothing, so the shell left the word alone and the correct pattern reached the tool, which is why a rehearsal at a different directory depth rehearsed something else. The remedy is to drive runCodemod from @storybook/codemod directly, which globs in process. The five converted files were reverted and the corpus was run again from the pre-conversion state.

CORRECTION. Formatting had been checked with node_modules/.bin/prettier, pinned at 2.1.2, and nothing in this repository runs that copy: .eslintrc extends eslint-config-prettier, which only switches formatting rules off, and nix fmt runs prettier 3.6.2. The wrong instrument had been in use for several tasks. It produced one divergence, a useEffect call in storybook/stories/_support/WithLocalState.tsx, corrected in its own commit ahead of this one. package.json still pins prettier at 2.1.2 while nix fmt runs 3.6.2; nothing reconciles the two.

compile moves from 68 TS2305 to 19 TS2339 in 8 files, all one shape: csf-2-to-3 cannot turn export const X = ImportedStory into an object literal, so it leaves X.parameters = {} and X.storyName = '' attached to a const TypeScript has typed as () => Element. The files are governance/DRepDirectory (2), governance/Delegation (1), notifications/Notifications (1), settings/language/Language (2), staking/RedeemItnRewards (8), staking/Staking (3), wallets/tokens/WalletTokens (1) and wallets/tokens/WalletTokensList (1), so four of the five tranches carry a share.

DECISION NEEDED IN task-018. lint moves from 0 errors to 49, all react/function-component-definition, across 25 files. Every one of the 49 is an export const X = () => ... story function; csf-2-to-3 leaves a plain story function as a function, which CSF 3 permits, and the rule objects to the arrow rather than to anything CSF asked for. The old .add('X', () => <Y />) form did not trigger it because the arrow sat in a call argument, which the rule does not inspect. Either the story functions take a form the rule accepts, or the rule is scoped off for story files. Measured: eslint --fix rewrites all 49 into export function X() { return ...; }, which the rule accepts and which leaves the export name, and so the derived label, untouched, so the first option is a mechanical pass rather than a rewrite. riskAreas: The container harness is the schedule for phases 6 and 7, not the screen count. research/05-reachable-screens.md section 7 establishes that one shared harness serves nearly every container, because all 48 screen containers read the same StoresMap through the same @inject decorator and none constructs a store or an Api of its own, with four named exceptions: SecuritySettingsPage, AnalyticsConsentPage, DRepDetailPage and LoadingPage. The 202 hours in phases 6 and 7 rest on that verdict. If it is wrong, and each container needs its own wiring, the figure is wrong by a wide margin rather than by a little.

Nothing in the corpus demonstrates a container fixture at screen scale. The only prior art is a 19-line literal at storybook/stories/nodes/_utils/props.ts covering the simplest container in the application. task-050 exists because the first wallet-scale story is the real proof, and task-049 records the tranche 1 to 5 rate so that proof can be measured against something.

strict: false gives the container work no help at all. tsconfig.json:79-85 disables strict and noImplicitAny and types/injectedPropsType.ts:6-10 types stores as any | StoresMap, so an incomplete fixture compiles and the first signal is a runtime failure in the story. Until task-057 lands, the only thing catching that is the per-tranche manual pass.

Request-shaped reads are the most likely repeated failure in container stories. Containers read isExecuting, error, wasExecuted, result and isExecutingFirstTime through without guarding, so an omitted field throws inside render rather than degrading. task-041 fixes it once in the harness default; found late, it is twelve separate fixes.

The 49 screens are not 49 stories. Twelve of them carry between two and six meaningful states each, and 90 to 120 stories is a planning estimate sensitive to how much dialog state is folded into a parent's stories rather than given its own.

The knob estimate is built from call-site counts, not from decisions. Of the 396 call sites in the corpus, 394 of them under storybook/stories, 204 sit at an indentation of eight spaces or deeper, meaning they are nested inside a callback, a mapped list or JSX and have no mechanical arg equivalent. They dominate phase 4 and are the largest source of error in the conversion half.

Phase 3 lands as one merge and no smaller unit is verifiable on the trunk. The mitigations are that everything version-neutral lands first in phases 1 and 2, that knobs and withState are untouched because addon-knobs 8.0.1 builds at 8.6.x, and that task-013 proves the runtime in a scratch worktree before the branch opens. The residual risk is review load on a single large landing.

react-polymorph 1.0.4 was last published 2022-04-14, the repository is read-only to us, and it sits between Storybook and every rendered story through StoryDecorator's ThemeProvider. Its behavior under a modern preview runtime has not been exercised. task-013 is the only place this surfaces before the bulk conversion.

The Storybook 10 target requires moving tsconfig moduleResolution off node, which changes resolution semantics for source/ as well as storybook/ because tsconfig.json carries no include. task-035 is the decision point, and 9.1.x is the documented fallback.

package.json:316 pins yarn@1.22.21 against a stated Storybook floor of yarn 4 from version 9, and Yarn 1 hoists flat, which is the shape that breaks a partially upgraded Storybook tree. The plan avoids storybook upgrade entirely and edits the manifest by hand, which removes the dependency on the least tested path but does not remove flat hoisting.

229 @ts-ignore directives across 48 story files are carried through the conversion by decision, so whatever they hide stays hidden. New container stories are written without them, which is the only place the count is held down.

storybook:build is wrapped x86_64-linux only, so nothing in this plan verifies the workbench builds on macOS or Windows. The operating-system switcher simulates platform chrome; it does not test a platform.

Provisional. The phase 4 tranches were rated against roughly 350 knob sites; the measured surface is about 410 (396 direct plus 44 indirect through loading/_support/loadingKnobs.ts, less 30 removed by the phase 1 deletions), which adds roughly 15 hours. task-050's acceptance re-estimates task-052, which is 36 hours already inside this total. task-039, named in riskAreas as the biggest unknown in the project, carries no risk premium over a mechanical task of the same size.
summary.testingNotes: No automated render check ships with this plan. @storybook/test-runner is out of scope per locked decision 7: it needs a Playwright browser and the Nix build is offline (nix/internal/common.nix:315). yarn compile proves every story type-checks, yarn lint proves it parses, yarn storybook:build proves the corpus bundles. None of them evaluates a preview module, so none proves a story renders. The container tranches in phases 6 and 7 are accepted by manual walkthrough.
summary.rollbackPlan: Phases 1 and 2 revert per task; reverting the glob restores the barrel. Phase 3 reverts as one merge, returning the repository to Storybook 6.4.22 with storiesOf intact and nothing later landed. Phase 4 reverts per tranche, with the 8 files carrying both knobs and withState coupled together. Phase 5 reverts to 8.6.x with a fully converted corpus, and the moduleResolution commit is separate because its fallout reaches source/. Phases 6 and 7 revert per tranche, since a screen story is purely additive. Phase 8 reverts per task. The state to avoid is a partially converted corpus with the manifest already bumped, which landing phase 3 as one merge makes unreachable on the trunk.
